newsitem.title: UK: Birds Eye aims to restore confidence in burgers.
newsitem.headline: Birds Eye aims to restore confidence in burgers.

text.p: Britain's' leading producer of frozen foods on Friday launched a campaign to restore consumer confidence in the beef burger market to counteract continuing fears about mad cow disease.
"There's been initiatives on fresh beef, but never before have there been initiatives on the beef burger market," a spokeswoman for Birds Eye, a unit of Unilever Plc, told Reuters.

Beef sales in Britain slumped sharply in March 1996 after the British government acknowledged there was a likely link between mad cow disease -- Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy -- and its fatal human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease.

Since then, the fresh beef market in Britain has substantially recovered, but the beef burger market has remained well below year-ago levels. The number of consumers claiming to buy fresh beef rose to 69 percent in December 1996 from 49 percent in March 1996. But the beef burger market remains 35 percent below March 1996 levels -- with the beef burger market in 1996 valued at about 139 million pounds ($225.2 million), compared to 200 million pounds in 1996, the Birds Eye spokeswoman said.
Consumers have shied away from beef burgers because they are cautious about buying minced beef as opposed to select cuts.
Birds Eye said is was just launching its "Commitment to Quality" campaign now, however, because it wanted to be able to assure consumers fully on the products they are buying.
"They wanted to be absolutely sure that the traceability on quality could be fully documented and demonstrated," the spokeswoman said.

The centrepiece of the campaign is a rosette insignia that is being placed on all Birds Eye beef burger products. The rosette denotes that the product is offal-free, is only from select cuts, comes from calves under 30 months old, and is all-British beef.
In-store leaflets and advertisements in leading consumer magazines will also be used to support the campaign, the spokeswoman said.
-- Leslie Adler, London Advertising Newsdesk +44 171 542 2815 ($ = 0.617 British Pounds)
